in the not-very-distant future, we
will be begging the people we are currently turning away to come and create
value in the US. Many people say we don’t need immigration
reform because people can work remotely.  While remote working works well
for a lot of companies, and I expect it to continue to work better as time goes
on, it doesn’t work well for all companies (for example, it would not work for
YC), and it shouldn’t be the only option.  It also sends money

text: out of the country rather than into it. A remote employee paid by an American firm keeps much of that pay where he or she already lives. The local market never receives the extra demand that an actual worker would bring. That is true in the small towns most likely to feel a labor shortage. Remote work remains a useful supplement but it cannot cover construction, manufacturing, or the face to face networks that YC and many other companies depend on. Treating it as a full substitute only makes the later shortage harder to repair in the end.
